column1: # Per-file real macOS bats wall time (seconds), used by shard-tests.sh to
# weight the CI partition by measured cost instead of @test count (#1243).
# @test count is a loose, occasionally blind proxy for a file's real cost:
# a file whose time is almost entirely waiting (background processes, poll
# loops) can carry a tiny count while dominating its shard's wall clock, and
# a file that is merely large in @test count is not necessarily slow. This
# table sidesteps the proxy by using each file's own measured time directly.
# MEASURED AGAINST: the macOS bats-timings artifacts of the five shards of
# tests.yml run 44470416041 (2026-11-19, head 1c44e063, all green), pinned by
# artifact id so the numbers can be regenerated exactly:
# Each row is that run's elapsed time for the file (file_end rows, status 0,
# macOS). This run (head 1c44e063) removed the BATS_TEST_TIMEOUT stalls from
# suites that call teardown_test_env, so those rows no longer contain the 180 s
# a stubbed kill() added to a file. test_state_root.bats and test_install.bats
# have their own teardown and still held such stalls at that head: their rows
# may be longer than their real cost and are re-measured at the next refresh.
#     END { for (k in m) print k "\t" m[k] }' */bats-timings.tsv | LC_ALL=C sort
# WHY THIS REFRESH (2026-11-20): with five macOS shards the previous table
# planned 1413-1457 s per shard, but a run measured 1075-1612 s: the table
# carried time that no longer exists (files that ran faster once nothing waited
# for bats' timeout watcher) and missed files added since. Re-planned from this
